context:
Goal: guards stop mistakes Claude is likely to make, and cost less than the harm they stop.
Problem (rule): You said keep the guard only if a replay shows no false refusals and the build is small. The lane measured the build: about 275 added hook lines plus 755 test lines, as a 38-commit stack on an old base that must be rebuilt on main (the lane's numbers, unchecked by triage). The replay needs a session on your computer, since the real runner commands are in your batch-runner transcripts there; guard.log lists refusals only, so it cannot give a false-refusal rate. By these numbers the build is not small.
Based on (measured): the lane's count, via the coordinator 18:32 CST Nov 13.
Departs from: main, which has none of this guard; a drops it and closes the stack's PRs, b keeps it with a line limit you set.
Meanwhile: the lane builds and closes nothing until your answer.
home: ruling own-715-c-guard-replay; step runner-repos-in-parallel; lane runner-repos-in-parallel-rest

options.gain: Nothing to rebuild; no false-refusal risk.
options.label: Drop the guard and close the stack's PRs (the coordinator's reading; recommended)
options.lose: No guard against a runner dropping --root; no incident shows one.

options.gain: The guard comes back if the build fits your limit.
options.label: Keep it, and I tell you what small means in lines
options.lose: A rebuild on main plus a replay on your computer.

short: 715 follow-up: what counts as a small build for the guard?
title: Your pick keeps the merge-roots guard only if its build is small. It is about 275 lines. Drop it, or say what small means?
why: About 275 hook lines plus 755 test lines is not small, and no incident shows a runner dropping --root.
